children: Hungary's seasonally-adjusted Purchasing Managers' Index (PMI) inched down to 53.1 in October (HUPMI=ECI) from a revised 53.3 in September, the index publisher said on Monday.

The October figure was higher than a long-term monthly average of 52.4 and was also above an average October reading 50.5 in the past three years, the Association of Logistics, Purchasing and Inventory Management said.
"Survey respondents in October reported slower expansion of the manufacturing industry compared with the previous month," the index publisher said in a statement.
"As a comparison, in the same period of 2025 we could also see an expansion," they added.
The 50-point mark separates contraction from growth.
The index of new orders was lower but still showed growth. The production volume index was higher than in the previous month and showed expansion.
The index for purchase prices was higher and continued to show an intense rise in prices, the publisher said.
The employment index was up and showed expansion. The export and import indicators were both down but showed expansion.
